question: uniqueness
claim: Unique when attained for almost every sample on each fixed-count stratum with at least four levels or three equally replicated levels. One- and two-level samples never attain. In ordinary sample coordinates the result uses nonattainment at sizes one and two, equal counts at size three and at least four distinct levels almost everywhere at larger sizes. Not unique in general: with all coefficients free, one copy each of \(\pm 512\), 512 copies each of \(\pm 7/4\) and 5120 copies each of \(\pm 1\) have distinct reflected finite global maxima.
frontier: Formalize the three-equally-replicated-level width-score reconstruction and the digamma bound used at join contact and at two levels. Unequal three-level multiplicities and the number of reflected winning orbits remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: Unique when a positive finite fit is attained for almost every sample on each fixed-count stratum with at least three levels when the held shape is neither 1 nor 2. The exact maximizing set at shape 1 or 2 is the whole support-compatible location interval when feasible. At lambda=-1 and sigma=1 the sample (-80/9,80/9) has reflected co-winners as well. Not unique in general: the sample (-1/4,1/4) at held shape 3/2 and scale 1 has exactly two maximizing locations, -5/12 and 5/12.
frontier: Resolve remaining small-level critical and support-contact comparisons and classify exceptional nonuniform components.

question: uniqueness
claim: Unique when attained for almost every strictly interior sample on each count stratum with at least four levels. A strict witness above both faces gives finitely many maximizing powers, with a unique beta-shape fit at each. At upper shape one the finite score identifies only shape1 times shape3. With upper shape free, upper shape two at the same product and sufficiently large power strictly improves the likelihood at every strictly interior observation.
frontier: Finite/gamma comparisons by score incidence require six levels. Exact root order at face equality and the golden singleton remain open.
